label: TP
reason: User input flows directly to printf() format string sink. The replace() sanitization only triggers when param.length() > 1, but when param is null or length <= 1, bar retains original user input. Additionally, the replace() inserts literal "Z" characters rather than neutralizing format specifiers (%s, %n, etc.), so attackers can still exploit printf with crafted input.

evidence.note: user param flows to printf format string sink without effective neutralization
sanitize replaces chars with Z but does not remove format specifiers
